chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:
I asked him about reed mats that urine comes upon: is salat (prayer) valid on them when they have dried, without being washed? He said: “Yes, there is no problem.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: salat (prayer), whose validity is being asked about
key_terms.الْبَوَارِي: reed mats or woven floor mats
key_terms.الْبَوْلُ: urine, the impurity affecting the mat
key_terms.تُغْسَلَ: to be washed, whose absence is part of the question
key_terms.جَفَّتْ: became dry, the condition mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no problem; an expression of permissibility

ai.seo_question: Is salat (prayer) valid on a reed mat touched by urine after it has dried without washing?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying on reed mats affected by urine after they have dried without washing. It indicates the permissibility of performing salat (prayer) on such mats in this case, making it relevant to ritual purity and prayer rulings in Shiʿi fiqh.
